decision: Do not add a Windows Admin Center MCP adapter on the current supported contract surface. Continue using the specialized windows-mcp, hyperv-mcp and failovercluster-mcp backends.
reasons: Current Microsoft documentation presents Windows Admin Center primarily as a gateway that manages targets through remote PowerShell and WMI/WinRM rather than as a stable external automation API for third-party agents.

The Windows Admin Center gateway-plugin SDK documentation states that the developer tooling has not yet been updated for plug-ins compatible with the modernized .NET 8 gateway, so it is not a stable production contract for a new generic MCP backend.
Gateway access does not grant least-privilege target access; Microsoft documents that most Windows Admin Center tools require administrative permissions on managed targets.

Windows Admin Center target RBAC offers a Readers role for individual machines, but Microsoft documents that this RBAC model is not supported for cluster management, which makes it unsuitable as a uniform least-privilege replacement for the existing specialized Hyper-V and Failover Cluster MCPs.

A wrapper around the built-in PowerShell/WMI gateway would duplicate existing specialized adapters and risk becoming the generic PowerShell/admin proxy explicitly prohibited by the mcp-lib security model.
safe_existing_path: windows-mcp for bounded Windows host diagnostics
hyperv-mcp for bounded Hyper-V host/VM diagnostics
reconsider_only_if: Microsoft publishes a stable supported external Windows Admin Center gateway API for automation clients
the API has a documented least-privilege read-only authorization model covering required target types including clusters
the adapter materially reduces duplication without exposing arbitrary PowerShell, WMI, REST or administrative execution
prohibited: browser automation against Windows Admin Center
reverse-engineered or undocumented internal gateway endpoints
using gateway-user access as proof of least-privilege target authorization
